zh.title: 利雅得機場遇襲釀3死　沙烏地航空客機起火受損、多國航空公司停航
zh.summary: 利雅得機場10月8日遇襲，沙烏地民航總局證實3人死亡；沙烏地航空客機起火並嚴重受損，多國航空公司停航，機型與是否全損仍待官方確認。
body: 沙烏地阿拉伯首都利雅得的哈立德國王國際機場（RUH）於2026年10月8日遭到攻擊，一架沙烏地阿拉伯籍沙烏地航空（Saudia）客機在停靠航廈期間起火並嚴重受損。沙烏地民航總局於10月9日證實，兩起攻擊分別針對機場設施及沙烏地航空航機，造成3名沙烏地公民死亡，多名沙烏地籍及其他國籍人士受傷，傷勢由輕傷至重傷不等。
葉門胡塞組織宣稱對機場發動飛彈攻擊。路透社引述3名知情人士指出，受損客機可能遭攔截過程產生的碎片，或其他飛行物直接擊中，隨後起火；路透社核實的現場影片可見機場內出現火焰及濃黑煙。目前尚無足夠資訊確認航機遭直接命中的武器種類，也不能將此次航機損傷確定歸因於無人機撞擊。
航空旅遊媒體One Mile at a Time將受損航機辨識為空中巴士A320，並稱其遭到摧毀。不過，沙烏地航空尚未公布涉事航機的機型、註冊編號及詳細損傷評估，機身、機翼或引擎的受損範圍也未獲可靠報導具體說明。因此，現階段可確認的是一架客機起火並嚴重受損，是否構成全損或正式報廢，仍待航空公司或相關單位公布；另有兩架空中巴士客機受損的說法，目前亦未獲可靠來源證實。
沙烏地航空另證實，受損航機當時沒有旅客在機上，並公布罹難機長為Hamoud Ali al-Kalthami。公司未進一步說明機長當時所在位置及罹難經過，因此「機上沒有旅客」不代表航機周邊或機上沒有工作人員。
攻擊造成利雅得機場航班大幅中斷。航空分析公司Cirium的統計顯示，10月8日原定378班離場航班中，有169班取消或未執行，約占45%。多家外籍航空公司隨後宣布暫停服務，德國漢莎航空集團（Lufthansa Group）表示，旗下航空公司暫停利雅得航班至10月16日，原因為中東局勢的最新發展。

印度籍航空公司也調整營運。靛藍航空（IndiGo）宣布取消往返利雅得航班至10月9日；印度航空（Air India）與印度籍低成本航空公司阿卡薩航空（Akasa Air）則取消至10月10日。印度航空一架原由德里飛往利雅得的班機於10月8日折返德里，阿卡薩航空取消兩班原定服務。巴基斯坦籍巴基斯坦國際航空（Pakistan International Airlines）亦宣布因中東局勢暫停利雅得航班。
部分航空公司的停航安排早於此次攻擊。香港籍國泰航空（Cathay Pacific）已於9月28日公告，取消杜拜及利雅得客運航班至2027年1月31日，並向受影響旅客提供改期、改道或退票安排。這項公告有明確取消期限，不能描述為此次攻擊後才宣布的無限期停航。
沙烏地民航總局於10月9日表示，機場作業已恢復，航空交通回歸正常。不過，機場恢復運作與個別航空公司恢復航班仍是不同安排，各公司已宣布的取消期限須依後續公告確認。胡塞組織表示，攻擊與沙烏地支持葉門政府軍有關；沙烏地則稱其支持聯合國承認的葉門政府，協助奪回胡塞組織控制的地區。

en.title: Riyadh Airport Attacks Kill Three, Damage Saudia Aircraft and Trigger Airline Suspensions
en.summary: Saudi authorities confirmed three deaths after the October 8 attacks at Riyadh airport. A Saudia passenger aircraft caught fire and sustained extensive damage, while several international airlines suspended services.
body: King Khalid International Airport (RUH) in Riyadh, the capital of Saudi Arabia, came under attack on October 8, 2026. A passenger aircraft operated by Saudi Arabian flag carrier Saudia caught fire and sustained extensive damage while parked at an airport terminal. On October 9, Saudi Arabia's General Authority of Civil Aviation confirmed that two attacks, one targeting airport facilities and another a Saudia aircraft, killed three Saudi citizens and injured several Saudi and foreign nationals. Injuries ranged from minor to severe.

Yemen's Houthi movement claimed responsibility for a missile attack on the airport. Reuters cited three people briefed on the matter as saying that fragments from an interception, or another projectile striking the aircraft directly, may have caused the damage and subsequent fire. Video verified by Reuters showed flames and thick black smoke at the airport. There is not enough information to establish the type of weapon that may have directly struck the aircraft, and the damage cannot be conclusively attributed to a drone impact.

Aviation travel outlet One Mile at a Time identified the damaged aircraft as an Airbus A320 and described it as destroyed. However, Saudia has not announced the aircraft type, registration or a detailed damage assessment, and reliable reporting has not specified the extent of damage to the fuselage, wings or engines. What can currently be confirmed is that a passenger aircraft caught fire and sustained extensive damage. Whether it constitutes a total loss or will formally be written off remains subject to confirmation by the airline or relevant authorities. Claims that two additional Airbus passenger aircraft were damaged have also not been substantiated by reliable sources.

Saudia separately confirmed that there were no passengers aboard the damaged aircraft and identified the deceased captain as Hamoud Ali al-Kalthami. The airline did not explain where the captain was at the time or the circumstances of his death. The absence of passengers therefore does not establish that no personnel were aboard or near the aircraft.

The attacks severely disrupted Riyadh airport operations. Aviation analytics company Cirium reported that 169 of 378 departures scheduled for October 8 were canceled or did not operate, representing approximately 45%. Several foreign airlines subsequently suspended services. Germany's Lufthansa Group said its airlines would suspend Riyadh flights through October 16 because of the latest developments in the Middle East.

Indian airlines also adjusted operations. IndiGo canceled flights to and from Riyadh through October 9, while Air India and Indian low-cost carrier Akasa Air canceled services through October 10. An Air India flight from Delhi to Riyadh returned to Delhi on October 8, and Akasa Air canceled two scheduled services. Pakistan International Airlines, based in Pakistan, also announced the suspension of Riyadh flights because of the Middle East situation.

Some airline suspensions predated these attacks. Hong Kong-based Cathay Pacific announced on September 28 that its Dubai and Riyadh passenger flights were canceled through January 31, 2027, with rebooking, rerouting or refunds available to affected travelers. The announcement specifies an end date and should not be described as an indefinite suspension newly announced after this attack.

Saudi Arabia's General Authority of Civil Aviation said on October 9 that airport operations had resumed and air traffic had returned to normal. However, reopening the airport and resuming individual airlines' services are separate matters; the cancellation periods announced by each carrier remain subject to subsequent updates. The Houthis said the attacks were related to Saudi support for Yemeni government forces. Saudi Arabia says it supports Yemen's United Nations-recognized government in recapturing areas controlled by the Houthis.
